hypothesis: On a second model (Claude Sonnet 5.5) and with contract v2 (harder probes for systematic-debugging and test-driven-development), preloading a skill raises the pass rate on its own contract probes by at least 0.15 versus BOTH no skill and a different skill from the set.
decision_rule: Units: (skill, probe, rep). Two contrasts, each with_skill minus a control: without_skill, and random_skill (another skill from the set, seeded derangement). Units where any arm did not run are excluded. Cluster = (skill, probe); statistic = mean of cluster means; seeded percentile bootstrap over clusters, separate seeds per contrast. Pass iff excluded/units <= max_notrun AND for BOTH contrasts the lower bound of the (1 - alpha) interval > 0 AND the mean >= min_effect. Excluded fraction above max_notrun => NotRun. Otherwise Fail, which closes this experiment_id. No multiplicity correction is applied because Pass requires both contrasts (intersection-union test). Secondary, descriptive only: per-skill counts.
